post.description:
Issue a new credit card for an existing or a new cardholder. A detailed explanation of different types and statuses can be found in our [guides](/docs/card-entity) section. Hint: you can also [replace](./replace-card) an existing card instead.
If the cardholder is in the invited state at the time of issuing the card, we will park the card issuing request and automatically issue the card once the cardholder is active.
Please be aware that card issuing is (as many other processes in Pliant's API) an [asynchronous process](/docs/core-concepts#mutating-data-happens-asynchronously). This means you need to rely on the callback for the card being active, before you can start using it.

cardholderId.description: The id of the [cardholder](/docs/cardholder-entity) to issue the card for. This cardholder needs to have a phone number, otherwise 3DS security mechanism during a purchase will not work. If not provided, you must provide a `cardholder` object to create a new cardholder as part of the card issuing process.

organizationId.description: The ID of the organization to issue the card for.

cardAccountId.description: The ID of the [card account](/docs/card-account) to issue the card for. If not provided, the card will be issued for the default [card account](/docs/card-account) of the organization. If the given card account has `status` `SUPERSEDED`, the request is transparently resolved to its successor (`supersededBy`) and the response carries the id of that successor card account.

cardConfig.description:
The Pliant card configuration of this card.
This describes all features of this card in one single configuration, e.g. the type of the card and also the design of the card etc.
Please refer to the [guide section](/docs/card-entity) to learn more about possible values.

cardDesignId.description:
The unique identifier of the card design used for this card.
This field can only be set when creating virtual cards.
Available designs for a card config can be retrieved via the [available cards endpoint](/reference/get-available-cards).

label.description: Mandatory only for virtual cards with a `cardConfig` containing `VIRTUAL` or `TRAVEL`, the maximum length is 40 characters.

purpose.description: Mandatory only for virtual cards with `cardConfig` ending with `SINGLE_USE`

validityPeriod.description:
Number of months when card expires.
- Mandatory for `cardConfig` containing `VIRTUAL` and `TRAVEL`
- For `cardConfig` ending with `PHYSICAL` or `BLACK`: set to 36 months automatically
- For `cardConfig` ending with `SINGLE_USE`: set to 12 months automatically
- For `cardConfig` containing `INSURANCE`:
  - Physical insurance: set to 24 months automatically
  - Virtual insurance (excluding single-use): validated from enum, defaults to 36 months
  - Single-use insurance: set to 12 months automatically
For cards with fixed validity periods, user input is ignored.

validFrom.description: Optional field to describe a fixed date range in which the card is usable for purchases, replaces the `validityPeriod` if used. Outside of this date range, the card cannot be used for any purchases, only for zero-amount card-checks, and is shown with `status` `PENDING`. If not provided, the card is active immediately. Date needs to be provided as `yyyy-mm-dd` and is treated inclusive, meaning the provided date is already a valid day to use the card. If used, the parallel usage of card controls regarding `dates` and/or `times` is not allowed and the `validityPeriod` will be set to 36 months automatically. The earliest possible date is the current date. The `validFrom` date needs to be before the `validTo` date. The fields `validFrom`, `validTo` and `validTimezone` need to be used together, if used at all. This field can be [updated later](/reference/update-card-validity-period). This field must be `null` when issuing benefit cards.

validTo.description: Optional field to describe a fixed date range in which the card is usable for purchases, replaces the `validityPeriod` if used. After the specified date, the card is automatically terminated. If not provided, the card is active until the `validityPeriod` ends. Date needs to be provided as `yyyy-mm-dd` and is treated inclusive, meaning the card will be terminated one day after this date. If used, the parallel usage of card controls regarding `dates` and/or `times` is not allowed and the `validityPeriod` will be set to 36 months automatically. The earliest possible date is the current date. The latest possible date is the end date of the `validityPeriod`. The fields `validFrom`, `validTo` and `validTimezone` need to be used together, if used at all. This field can be [updated later](/reference/update-card-validity-period). This field must be `null` when issuing benefit cards.

validTimezone.description: Optional field to describe the timezone for the `validFrom` and `validTo` fields. This field is mandatory if `validFrom` and `validTo` fields are used. A list of valid timezones can be found in our [guide section](/docs/card-controls-1). This field can be [updated later](/reference/update-card-validity-period). This field must be `null` when issuing benefit cards.

maxTransactionCount.description:
:exclamation: IMPORTANT: if the `cardConfig` is `TRAVEL` and this field is not set, the **default value will be `5`**.
Optional field to describe the maximum number of transactions within the range of `1..999999999` that can be performed with this card.
If not provided, the card can be used for an unlimited number of transactions until the card expires.

limit.description: The limit of the card. The limit renews according to the `limitRenewFrequency` or never, if `limitRenewFrequency` is set to `TOTAL`. This limit can later be adjusted via the [update limit endpoint](/reference/update-card-limit). The limit can be up to the organization's overall limit. For instance an organization with a limit of 1,000,000 EUR can have a card with a limit up to 1,000,000 EUR. It is also possible to have more than one card with the maximum limit. For example you can have two cards each with a limit of 1,000,000 EUR. The card limits are not added up on creation, only the transactions happening on the card are added up and checked against the organization's overall limit. The limit must be `0` (of the card's currency) when issuing benefit cards.

value.description: The value of the monetary amount, converted to minor units of the currency. For instance 1.00 EUR is 100 cents, thus the value here is `100`. See our [guides](/docs/monetary-values) for more details about how to handle monetary amounts.

currency.description: The currency of the monetary amount in ISO 4217 format, for example `EUR` for Euro. This has to match the currency of the respective [card account](/docs/card-account)!

limitRenewFrequency.description:
The frequency of the card limit renewal.
* `DAILY` - The card limit is renewed every day
* `WEEKLY` - The card limit is renewed every week
* `MONTHLY` - The card limit is renewed every calendar month, this is the default setting.
* `QUARTERLY` - The card limit is renewed every calendar quarter.
* `ANNUAL` - The card limit is renewed every year.
* `TOTAL` - The card limit is never going to be renewed. After the limit is spent the card cannot be used anymore.

transactionLimit.description: The transaction limit of the card. Meaning the maximum amount of a single transaction. This is always below or equal to the `limit` of the card. This limit can later be adjusted via the [update limit endpoint](/reference/update-card-limit). The transaction limit can be up to the card's limit. For instance a card with a limit of 1,000 EUR can have a transaction limit up to 1,000 EUR. The transaction limit must be `0` (of the card's currency) when issuing benefit cards.

value.description: The value of the monetary amount, converted to minor units of the currency. For instance 1.00 EUR is 100 cents, thus the value here is `100`. See our [guides](/docs/monetary-values) for more details about how to handle monetary amounts.

currency.description: The currency of the monetary amount in ISO 4217 format, for example `EUR` for Euro. This has to match the currency of the respective [card account](/docs/card-account)!

customFirstName.description: Optional first name on `TRAVEL` cards which will be used on the card. When used, this replaces the [cardholder](/docs/cardholder-entity) first name, which normally is used on the card. The maximum length of `customFirstName` is 50 characters. If used, both fields (`customFirstName` and `customLastName`) have to be provided with at least one character each. It is important to note, that only the following characters are allowed for issuing cards: `A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`, `äöüÄÖÜ.-`

customLastName.description: Optional last name on `TRAVEL` cards which will be used on the card. When used, this replaces the [cardholder](/docs/cardholder-entity) last name, which normally is used on the card. The maximum length of `customLastName` is 50 characters. If used, both fields (`customFirstName` and `customLastName`) have to be provided with at least one character each. It is important to note, that only the following characters are allowed for issuing cards: `A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`, `äöüÄÖÜ.-`

cardControls.description: Optionally, the card controls which will be applied to this card.

customFields.description: Optional custom fields which can be set on a card. A custom field may have a default value which will be copied to every transaction made with this card. You can identify a custom field either by its `id` or its `label`. If both are provided, the `id` will be used. You can also create new custom fields (of type `TEXT`) on-the-fly by providing a newly, unused label and the corresponding default value you want to set. So mainly two uses cases exist: 1. Use an existing custom field on the card, mostly identified via its `id`. 2. Create a new custom field (of type `TEXT`) on-the-fly via the `label` and set it on the card.

id.description: The id of the custom field, to identify an existing custom field which should be set on this card. Either `id` or `label` has to be provided. If both are provided, the `id` will be used.

label.description: The label of the custom field, to identify which custom field should be set on this card. Or, to create a new custom field on-the-fly, if the label is currently unused. Either `id` or `label` has to be provided. If both are provided, the `id` will be used.

defaultValue.description: The default value of the custom field to set on this card. This default value will be copied to every transaction made with this card. This is not the default value of the custom field itself, but the default value of the custom field on this card! The maximum length of the default value is 64kB.

deliverTo.description:
Optionally, specifies where the physical card should be delivered.
* `ORGANIZATION` - Ship to organization address (default)
* `CARDHOLDER` - Ship to cardholder's personal delivery address

This field is only applicable for physical cards.
If not provided, the card will be shipped to the organization address.


The request will fail if the cardholder's personal delivery address is not set and `deliverTo` is set to `CARDHOLDER`.

cardholder.description: Optional description of a new [cardholder](/docs/cardholder-entity) to be created alongside the card. If `cardholderId` is not provided, this field is required.

membershipType.description:
Defines how the cardholder is onboarded and accesses their cards.
`STANDARD` - Cardholders receive an invitation email to register, set up a password and MFA, and become registered members with access to the Pliant web app according to their assigned role.
`LIMITED` - For distributing cards via access links without requiring registration. This is also intended for direct customers sharing cards with recipients outside their organization. Cardholders do not receive a registration invitation and cannot access the Pliant web app. Instead, they access their cards through access links shared with them, with access limited to card-related functionality. The `GUEST` role is assigned automatically and does not need to be provided.
`EMBEDDED` - Reserved for partners embedding the cardholder experience in their own application. No invitation email is sent. The partner is responsible for obtaining acceptance of the terms and conditions and verifying the cardholder's phone number.
If not provided, `STANDARD` is applied. `LIMITED` and `EMBEDDED` always have to be requested explicitly.

salutation.description: The Salutation used for email communication.

email.description: The email address of the cardholder. This will be used for email communication. If a cardholder with this email address already exists, all the information from the existing cardholder will be used, the cardholder information sent in this request will be ignored.

firstName.description: The first name of the cardholder. This will be printed on credit cards as the cardholder. It is important to note, that only the following characters are allowed for issuing cards: `A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`, `äöüÄÖÜ.-` The combined length of first name and last name must not exceed 24 characters. One additional character is reserved for the space inserted between them when displayed on the card (25 characters in total).

lastName.description: The last name of the cardholder. This will be printed on credit cards as the cardholder. It is important to note, that only the following characters are allowed for issuing cards: `A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`, `äöüÄÖÜ.-` The combined length of first name and last name must not exceed 24 characters. One additional character is reserved for the space inserted between them when displayed on the card (25 characters in total).

language.description: Used for setting the language in Pliant apps as well as for email communication.

nationality.description: The nationality of the cardholder (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2).

roles.description:

Required for `STANDARD` memberships. For `LIMITED` the `GUEST` role is assigned automatically and cannot be combined with any other role, so you do not need to provide this property. For `EMBEDDED` roles do not apply and `CARDHOLDER` is used when none is provided.

If used, the parallel usage of card controls regarding `dates` and/or `times` is not allowed and the `validityPeriod` will be set to 36 months automatically. The latest possible date is the end date of the `validityPeriod`. The fields `validFrom`, `validTo` and `validTimezone` need to be used together, if used at all.

validTimezone.description: Optional field to describe the timezone for the `validFrom` and `validTo` fields. This field is mandatory if `validFrom` and `validTo` fields are used. A list of valid timezones can be found in our [guide section](/docs/card-controls-1).

maxTransactionCount.description: Optional field to describe the maximum number of transactions within the range of `1..999999999` that can be performed with this card. If not provided, the card can be used for an unlimited number of transactions until the card expires.

clickToPayInfo.description:
Click to Pay enrollment information for this card. Only present for Visa cards that support Click to Pay.
This object may be `null` if Click to Pay is not supported generally (e.g., per country), but normally it will be present with a `status` of `NOT_SUPPORTED` if the card type doesn't support Click to Pay (e.g., Mastercard or Travel Purchasing Cards).

status.description:
The Click to Pay enrollment status of the card.
* `NOT_SUPPORTED` - Card type doesn't support Click to Pay (e.g., Mastercard or Travel Purchasing Cards)
* `NOT_ENROLLED` - Card is eligible but not enrolled in Click to Pay
* `PENDING` - Card enrollment is awaiting the cardholder's Click to Pay member enrollment to complete
* `ENROLLED` - Card is currently enrolled in Click to Pay

x-enumDescriptions.NOT_SUPPORTED: Card type doesn't support Click to Pay (e.g., Mastercard or Travel Purchasing Cards).
x-enumDescriptions.NOT_ENROLLED: Card is eligible but not enrolled in Click to Pay.
x-enumDescriptions.PENDING: Card enrollment is awaiting the cardholder's Click to Pay member enrollment to complete. Once the member is enrolled, the card enrollment is triggered automatically.
x-enumDescriptions.ENROLLED: Card is currently enrolled in Click to Pay.

enrolledAt.description: Date-time when the card was enrolled in Click to Pay. `null` if the card has never been enrolled.

unenrolledAt.description: Date-time when the card was unenrolled from Click to Pay. `null` if the card has never been unenrolled.

customFields.description: The [custom fields](/docs/custom-fields-on-transactions) set on this card. These [custom fields](/docs/custom-fields-on-transactions) are used as default values for every transaction made with this card. If no [custom fields](/docs/custom-fields-on-transactions) are assigned to the card, we return an empty list.

copilots.description: Optional feature for `TRAVEL` cards. The copilot also has access to the card and its card details alongside with the cardholder of the card itself.

cardholderIds.description: The IDs of the cardholders assigned as copilots to the card.

teamIds.description: The IDs of the teams assigned as copilots to the card.

additionalLimits.description: Additional limits set on the card. Empty when none were configured at creation.

items.description: An additional limit applied to this card.

id.description: The unique identifier of this additional limit. Use this `id` when updating or removing the limit via `PUT /api/cards/limits/{cardId}`.

limitRenewFrequency.description:
The renewal frequency of this additional limit. `PER_TRANSACTION` is only valid for additional limits, not for the card's primary limit.
* `PER_TRANSACTION` - Limit applies to each individual transaction.
* `DAILY` - The limit is renewed every day.
* `WEEKLY` - The limit is renewed every week.
* `MONTHLY` - The limit is renewed every calendar month.
* `QUARTERLY` - The limit is renewed every calendar quarter.
* `ANNUAL` - The limit is renewed every year.
* `TOTAL` - The limit is never renewed. Once spent, no further transactions are allowed under this limit.

limit.description: The monetary cap for this additional limit.

value.description: The value of the monetary amount, converted to minor units of the currency. For instance 1.00 EUR is 100 cents, thus the value here is `100`. See our [guides](/docs/monetary-values) for more details about how to handle monetary amounts.

currency.description: The currency of the monetary amount in ISO 4217 format, for example `EUR` for Euro or `USD` for US Dollar.

maxTransactionCount.description: Maximum number of transactions allowed under this additional limit within its renewal period. Null if no transaction-count cap is configured.

scope.description: The scope restriction of this additional limit. Null when no scope is defined (`categories` and `acceptanceMethods` empty, `atmWithdrawal` false, `currency` null).

categories.description: Merchant category types this limit applies to. Empty when no category restriction is set.

acceptanceMethods.description: The card acceptance methods this limit applies to. Empty when no acceptance-method restriction is set.

atmWithdrawal.description: When `true`, this additional limit applies to ATM withdrawal transactions.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code this limit is scoped to, e.g. `PLN`. Null when no currency scope is defined.

balanceInfo.description: Spending balance information for this additional limit. Null when no balance record exists.

balance.description: Amount spent under this additional limit in the current renewal period.

value.description: The value of the monetary amount, converted to minor units of the currency. For instance 1.00 EUR is 100 cents, thus the value here is `100`. See our [guides](/docs/monetary-values) for more details about how to handle monetary amounts.

currency.description: The currency of the monetary amount in ISO 4217 format, for example `EUR` for Euro or `USD` for US Dollar.

availableLimit.description: Remaining amount available under this additional limit in the current renewal period.

value.description: The value of the monetary amount, converted to minor units of the currency. For instance 1.00 EUR is 100 cents, thus the value here is `100`. See our [guides](/docs/monetary-values) for more details about how to handle monetary amounts.

currency.description: The currency of the monetary amount in ISO 4217 format, for example `EUR` for Euro or `USD` for US Dollar.

limitRenewDate.description: Date when this additional limit's balance will next be renewed, e.g. `2026-06-01`. Null for `TOTAL` frequency limits.

404.description: Not Found. The requested resource could not be found.

422.description: Unprocessable Content. The request could not be completed due to contents of the request. The syntax of the request content was correct.

post.description: Creates a new card account for the specified organization.

organizationId.description: The unique identifier of the organization.

name.description: The name of the card account.

currency.description: The currency code (e.g., EUR, USD).

id.description: The id of the card account.

organizationId.description: The id of the organization this card account belongs to.

name.description: The name of the card account.

purpose.description: Optionally, a description of the purpose of the card account.

status.description:
The status of the card account.
  - `ACTIVE` - the card account is operational.
  - `PENDING` - the card account is not operational yet, e.g. because the organization is still onboarding.
  - `DEACTIVATED` - the card account was deactivated and can no longer be used.
  - `CANCELLED` - the card account was cancelled.
  - `SUPERSEDED` - the card account was replaced by a successor card account and is kept for historical reasons only.
    It stays readable, but no new cards, payments or payouts can be created on it. The successor is referenced by `supersededBy`.
    See the [card account guide](/docs/card-account) for details.

currency.description: The currency of the card account.

bankAccountInformation.description: The Pliant-internal bank account information of the card account. This is the bank account where the balance of the card account is kept. This bank account is also used for adding top-up payments to the card account, if it is a prefund or hybrid card account. One card account can have multiple bank accounts. Non-active organizations might not have bank account information. The bank account is Pliant-internal, for the external bank account information see the [separate endpoint](/reference/get-organizations-external-bank-accounts).

transferType.description:
Flag that indicates which payment rail the processing account is configured for.
  - `SWIFT` - transfers routed through the SWIFT network.
  - `LOCAL` - domestic rails such as UK's Faster Payments.
Depending on this flag, other fields are set or not, e.g. `bic` and `iban` for `SWIFT`, `sortCode` and `accountNumber` for `LOCAL` in case of UK Faster Payments.
The field might be `null` or empty, in which case `SWIFT` should be assumed.

beneficiary.description: The beneficiary of the bank account. This is the name of the account holder.

bankName.description: The name of the bank of the bank account.

bic.description: The BIC of the bank account. This is the bank identifier code. For backward compatibility reasons this field is never `null`, but depending on `transferType` it can be empty. In future iterations it will become optional.

iban.description: The IBAN of the bank account. This is the international bank account number. For backward compatibility reasons this field is never `null`, but depending on `transferType` it can be empty. In future iterations it will become optional.

sortCode.description: Bank identifier that accompanies the beneficiary account. Only set for certain `transferType` values, e.g. UK Faster Payments.

accountNumber.description: Account identifier for the beneficiary account. Only set for certain `transferType` values, e.g. UK Faster Payments.

defaultAccount.description: Indicates whether this is the default card account. There is always one active default card account.

accountType.description: The account type of the card account.

creditLimit.description: The credit limit of the card account. The credit limit is the maximum amount of money that can be spent with all cards of this card account. It is always less or equal to the overall credit limit of the organization. Meaning all card accounts share the same organization credit limit. This organization credit limit can be distributed among the card accounts. Only relevant for `CREDIT`-based card accounts.

availableLimit.description: The remaining available credit limit of the card account. The available credit limit is the maximum amount of money that can be spent with all cards of this card account. For `PREFUNDED` card accounts, the available credit limit is the remaining balance of the card account.

balance.description: The remaining balance of the card account.

paymentFrequency.description: The payment frequency of the card account. This is the frequency with which the card account is settled for this organization. Only relevant for `CREDIT`-based card accounts.

paymentDefermentInDays.description: The payment deferment in days of the card account. Only relevant for `CREDIT`-based card accounts.

activatedAt.description: The date and time when the card account was activated.

createdAt.description: The date and time when the card account was created.

supersededBy.description: The id of the card account that took over from this one. Only set if this card account has `status` `SUPERSEDED`, `null` otherwise. Follow this id to find the card account that holds the current balance, limits and bank account information.

supersedes.description: The id of the card account this one took over from. Only set if this card account is the successor of a superseded card account, `null` otherwise. The superseded card account remains readable and keeps its historical transactions, statements and account entries.

supersededAt.description: The date and time when this card account was superseded. Only set together with `supersededBy`, `null` otherwise.

benefitCardAccount.description: Set to true for the card account that is dedicated to funding benefit cards.

409.description: Conflict. The request could not be completed due to a conflict with the current state of the resource. You may retry the call.

get.description:
Returns a list of cards. You can use the `limit`, `page`, `sortBy` and `sortDirection` parameters to filter and sort the results.

**This endpoint has changed in comparison to the previous version of the API.** The following changes were made:
- changed the enumeration for the status field in the response body

parameters.name: organizationId
parameters.description: The ID of the organization to filter by.

parameters.name: cardAccountId
parameters.description: The ID of the card account to filter by. A card always carries the card account it is currently assigned to. Once a card has been reassigned (see the `CARD_REASSIGNED` callback), it is only returned for its new card account, not for the superseded one.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: A list of statuses of cards to filter by.

parameters.name: cardholderId
parameters.description: The ID of the [cardholder](/docs/cardholder-entity) to filter by.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: **DEPRECATED**: Use `cardConfig` parameter instead. A list of types of cards to filter by.

parameters.name: cardConfig
parameters.description: Filter by exact card configuration (e.g., PLIANT_PHYSICAL, PLIANT_VIRTUAL_TRAVEL, PLIANT_SINGLE_USE). Can be specified multiple times for filtering by multiple configurations.

parameters.name: fromDate
parameters.description: The `from` date to filter by as zero-offset UTC time. The date boundary is inclusive. Meaning we compare with `>=`.

parameters.name: toDate
parameters.description: The `to` date to filter by as zero-offset UTC time. The date boundary is inclusive. Meaning we compare with `<=`.

parameters.name: byDateField
parameters.description: The date field to filter by if `fromDate` and `toDate` are present.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of items to return per page. The default value if not provided is 100, the maximum allowed value is 1000.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page number to return, starting with 0, this counts up to the total number of pages. The total number of pages is determined by the total number of records divided by the limit.

parameters.name: sortBy
parameters.description: The field to sort by.

parameters.name: sortDirection
parameters.description: The direction to sort by.

cardId.description: The unique identifier of the card.

organizationId.description: The unique identifier of the organization.

cardAccountId.description: The unique identifier of the card account.

cardholderId.description: The unique identifier of the cardholder.

type.description:
Deprecated, please use `cardConfig` instead.
`VIRTUAL` - Virtual credit card
`SINGLE_USE` - One-time virtual credit card (only one authorization allowed per card)
`PHYSICAL` - Physical credit card
`BLACK` - Physical black premium credit card
`TRAVEL` - Virtual cards used specifically in travel industry related use cases

cardConfig.description: The Pliant card configuration of this card. This describes all feature of this card in one single configuration, e.g. the type of the card and also the design of the card etc. It replaces the deprecated card `type`. Please refer to the [guide section](/docs/card-entity) to learn more about possible values.

platformFee.description: Whether the card is used for the internal Pliant platform fee or not.

cardDesignId.description: The unique identifier of the card design used for this specific card.

cardDesignLogoName.description: The name of the card design used for this specific card.

createdAt.description: The date-time when card was created.

updatedAt.description: The date-time when card was updated.

hasNextPage.description: Indicates whether there is a next page available.

403.description: Forbidden. The API consumer is not allowed to access the requested resource.

429.description: Too Many Requests. The API consumer has sent too many requests in a given amount of time. Please check our [API guidelines](/docs/pliant-api-guidelines#api-rate-limits).

error.description: Detailed description of the error and breached rate limit.

500.description: Internal Server Error. The request was not completed due to an internal error.

post.description:
Issue a new credit card for an existing or a new cardholder. A detailed explanation of different types and statuses can be found in our [guides](/docs/card-entity) section. Hint: you can also [replace](./replace-card) an existing card instead.
If the cardholder is in the invited state at the time of issuing the card, we will park the card issuing request and automatically issue the card once the cardholder is active.
Please be aware that card issuing is (as many other processes in Pliant's API) an [asynchronous process](/docs/core-concepts#mutating-data-happens-asynchronously). This means you need to rely on the callback for the card being active, before you can start using it.

cardholderId.description: The id of the [cardholder](/docs/cardholder-entity) to issue the card for. This cardholder needs to have a phone number, otherwise 3DS security mechanism during a purchase will not work. If not provided, you must provide a `cardholder` object to create a new cardholder as part of the card issuing process.

organizationId.description: The ID of the organization to issue the card for.

cardAccountId.description: The ID of the [card account](/docs/card-account) to issue the card for. If not provided, the card will be issued for the default [card account](/docs/card-account) of the organization. If the given card account has `status` `SUPERSEDED`, the request is transparently resolved to its successor (`supersededBy`) and the response carries the id of that successor card account.

cardConfig.description:
The Pliant card configuration of this card.
This describes all features of this card in one single configuration, e.g. the type of the card and also the design of the card etc.
Please refer to the [guide section](/docs/card-entity) to learn more about possible values.

cardDesignId.description:
The unique identifier of the card design used for this card.
This field can only be set when creating virtual cards.
Available designs for a card config can be retrieved via the [available cards endpoint](/reference/get-available-cards).

label.description: Mandatory only for virtual cards with a `cardConfig` containing `VIRTUAL` or `TRAVEL`, the maximum length is 40 characters.

purpose.description: Mandatory only for virtual cards with `cardConfig` ending with `SINGLE_USE`

validityPeriod.description:
Number of months when card expires.
- Mandatory for `cardConfig` containing `VIRTUAL` and `TRAVEL`
- For `cardConfig` ending with `PHYSICAL` or `BLACK`: set to 36 months automatically
- For `cardConfig` ending with `SINGLE_USE`: set to 12 months automatically
- For `cardConfig` containing `INSURANCE`:
  - Physical insurance: set to 24 months automatically
  - Virtual insurance (excluding single-use): validated from enum, defaults to 36 months
  - Single-use insurance: set to 12 months automatically
For cards with fixed validity periods, user input is ignored.

validFrom.description: Optional field to describe a fixed date range in which the card is usable for purchases, replaces the `validityPeriod` if used. Outside of this date range, the card cannot be used for any purchases, only for zero-amount card-checks, and is shown with `status` `PENDING`. If not provided, the card is active immediately. Date needs to be provided as `yyyy-mm-dd` and is treated inclusive, meaning the provided date is already a valid day to use the card. If used, the parallel usage of card controls regarding `dates` and/or `times` is not allowed and the `validityPeriod` will be set to 36 months automatically. The earliest possible date is the current date. The `validFrom` date needs to be before the `validTo` date. The fields `validFrom`, `validTo` and `validTimezone` need to be used together, if used at all. This field can be [updated later](/reference/update-card-validity-period). This field must be `null` when issuing benefit cards.

validTo.description: Optional field to describe a fixed date range in which the card is usable for purchases, replaces the `validityPeriod` if used. After the specified date, the card is automatically terminated. If not provided, the card is active until the `validityPeriod` ends. Date needs to be provided as `yyyy-mm-dd` and is treated inclusive, meaning the card will be terminated one day after this date. If used, the parallel usage of card controls regarding `dates` and/or `times` is not allowed and the `validityPeriod` will be set to 36 months automatically. The earliest possible date is the current date. The latest possible date is the end date of the `validityPeriod`. The fields `validFrom`, `validTo` and `validTimezone` need to be used together, if used at all. This field can be [updated later](/reference/update-card-validity-period). This field must be `null` when issuing benefit cards.

validTimezone.description: Optional field to describe the timezone for the `validFrom` and `validTo` fields. This field is mandatory if `validFrom` and `validTo` fields are used. A list of valid timezones can be found in our [guide section](/docs/card-controls-1). This field can be [updated later](/reference/update-card-validity-period). This field must be `null` when issuing benefit cards.

maxTransactionCount.description:
:exclamation: IMPORTANT: if the `cardConfig` is `TRAVEL` and this field is not set, the **default value will be `5`**.
Optional field to describe the maximum number of transactions within the range of `1..999999999` that can be performed with this card.
If not provided, the card can be used for an unlimited number of transactions until the card expires.

limit.description: The limit of the card. The limit renews according to the `limitRenewFrequency` or never, if `limitRenewFrequency` is set to `TOTAL`. This limit can later be adjusted via the [update limit endpoint](/reference/update-card-limit). The limit can be up to the organization's overall limit. For instance an organization with a limit of 1,000,000 EUR can have a card with a limit up to 1,000,000 EUR. It is also possible to have more than one card with the maximum limit. For example you can have two cards each with a limit of 1,000,000 EUR. The card limits are not added up on creation, only the transactions happening on the card are added up and checked against the organization's overall limit. The limit must be `0` (of the card's currency) when issuing benefit cards.

value.description: The value of the monetary amount, converted to minor units of the currency. For instance 1.00 EUR is 100 cents, thus the value here is `100`. See our [guides](/docs/monetary-values) for more details about how to handle monetary amounts.

currency.description: The currency of the monetary amount in ISO 4217 format, for example `EUR` for Euro. This has to match the currency of the respective [card account](/docs/card-account)!

limitRenewFrequency.description:
The frequency of the card limit renewal.
* `DAILY` - The card limit is renewed every day
* `WEEKLY` - The card limit is renewed every week
* `MONTHLY` - The card limit is renewed every calendar month, this is the default setting.
* `QUARTERLY` - The card limit is renewed every calendar quarter.
* `ANNUAL` - The card limit is renewed every year.
* `TOTAL` - The card limit is never going to be renewed. After the limit is spent the card cannot be used anymore.

transactionLimit.description: The transaction limit of the card. Meaning the maximum amount of a single transaction. This is always below or equal to the `limit` of the card. This limit can later be adjusted via the [update limit endpoint](/reference/update-card-limit). The transaction limit can be up to the card's limit. For instance a card with a limit of 1,000 EUR can have a transaction limit up to 1,000 EUR. The transaction limit must be `0` (of the card's currency) when issuing benefit cards.

value.description: The value of the monetary amount, converted to minor units of the currency. For instance 1.00 EUR is 100 cents, thus the value here is `100`. See our [guides](/docs/monetary-values) for more details about how to handle monetary amounts.

currency.description: The currency of the monetary amount in ISO 4217 format, for example `EUR` for Euro. This has to match the currency of the respective [card account](/docs/card-account)!

customFirstName.description: Optional first name on `TRAVEL` cards which will be used on the card. When used, this replaces the [cardholder](/docs/cardholder-entity) first name, which normally is used on the card. The maximum length of `customFirstName` is 50 characters. If used, both fields (`customFirstName` and `customLastName`) have to be provided with at least one character each. It is important to note, that only the following characters are allowed for issuing cards: `A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`, `äöüÄÖÜ.-`

customLastName.description: Optional last name on `TRAVEL` cards which will be used on the card. When used, this replaces the [cardholder](/docs/cardholder-entity) last name, which normally is used on the card. The maximum length of `customLastName` is 50 characters. If used, both fields (`customFirstName` and `customLastName`) have to be provided with at least one character each. It is important to note, that only the following characters are allowed for issuing cards: `A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`, `äöüÄÖÜ.-`

cardControls.description: Optionally, the card controls which will be applied to this card.

customFields.description: Optional custom fields which can be set on a card. A custom field may have a default value which will be copied to every transaction made with this card. You can identify a custom field either by its `id` or its `label`. If both are provided, the `id` will be used. You can also create new custom fields (of type `TEXT`) on-the-fly by providing a newly, unused label and the corresponding default value you want to set. So mainly two uses cases exist: 1. Use an existing custom field on the card, mostly identified via its `id`. 2. Create a new custom field (of type `TEXT`) on-the-fly via the `label` and set it on the card.

id.description: The id of the custom field, to identify an existing custom field which should be set on this card. Either `id` or `label` has to be provided. If both are provided, the `id` will be used.

label.description: The label of the custom field, to identify which custom field should be set on this card. Or, to create a new custom field on-the-fly, if the label is currently unused. Either `id` or `label` has to be provided. If both are provided, the `id` will be used.

defaultValue.description: The default value of the custom field to set on this card. This default value will be copied to every transaction made with this card. This is not the default value of the custom field itself, but the default value of the custom field on this card! The maximum length of the default value is 64kB.

teamId.description: The ID of the team to issue the card for.

projectId.description: The ID of the project to issue the card for.

copilots.description: Optional feature for `TRAVEL` cards. This feature allows to assign cardholders or teams as copilots to the card. The copilot also has access to the card and its card details alongside with the cardholder of the card itself.

cardholderIds.description: The IDs of the cardholders to assign as copilot to the card.

teamIds.description: The IDs of the teams to assign as copilot to the card.

deliverTo.description:
Optionally, specifies where the physical card should be delivered.
* `ORGANIZATION` - Ship to organization address (default)
* `CARDHOLDER` - Ship to cardholder's personal delivery address

This field is only applicable for physical cards.
If not provided, the card will be shipped to the organization address.


The request will fail if the cardholder's personal delivery address is not set and `deliverTo` is set to `CARDHOLDER`.

cardholder.description: Optional description of a new [cardholder](/docs/cardholder-entity) to be created alongside the card. If `cardholderId` is not provided, this field is required.

membershipType.description:
Defines how the cardholder is onboarded and accesses their cards.
`STANDARD` - Cardholders receive an invitation email to register, set up a password and MFA, and become registered members with access to the Pliant web app according to their assigned role.
`LIMITED` - For distributing cards via access links without requiring registration. This is also intended for direct customers sharing cards with recipients outside their organization. Cardholders do not receive a registration invitation and cannot access the Pliant web app. Instead, they access their cards through access links shared with them, with access limited to card-related functionality. The `GUEST` role is assigned automatically and does not need to be provided.
`EMBEDDED` - Reserved for partners embedding the cardholder experience in their own application. No invitation email is sent. The partner is responsible for obtaining acceptance of the terms and conditions and verifying the cardholder's phone number.
If not provided, `STANDARD` is applied. `LIMITED` and `EMBEDDED` always have to be requested explicitly.

salutation.description: The Salutation used for email communication.

email.description: The email address of the cardholder. This will be used for email communication. If a cardholder with this email address already exists, all the information from the existing cardholder will be used, the cardholder information sent in this request will be ignored.

firstName.description: The first name of the cardholder. This will be printed on credit cards as the cardholder. It is important to note, that only the following characters are allowed for issuing cards: `A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`, `äöüÄÖÜ.-` The combined length of first name and last name must not exceed 24 characters. One additional character is reserved for the space inserted between them when displayed on the card (25 characters in total).

lastName.description: The last name of the cardholder. This will be printed on credit cards as the cardholder. post.description:
Issue a new credit card for an existing or a new cardholder. A detailed explanation of different types and statuses can be found in our [guides](/docs/card-entity) section. Hint: you can also [replace](./replace-card) an existing card instead.
If the cardholder is in the invited state at the time of issuing the card, we will park the card issuing request and automatically issue the card once the cardholder is active.
Please be aware that card issuing is (as many other processes in Pliant's API) an [asynchronous process](/docs/core-concepts#mutating-data-happens-asynchronously). This means you need to rely on the callback for the card being active, before you can start using it.

cardholderId.description: The id of the [cardholder](/docs/cardholder-entity) to issue the card for. This cardholder needs to have a phone number, otherwise 3DS security mechanism during a purchase will not work. If not provided, you must provide a `cardholder` object to create a new cardholder as part of the card issuing process.

organizationId.description: The ID of the organization to issue the card for.

cardAccountId.description: The ID of the [card account](/docs/card-account) to issue the card for. If not provided, the card will be issued for the default [card account](/docs/card-account) of the organization. If the given card account has `status` `SUPERSEDED`, the request is transparently resolved to its successor (`supersededBy`) and the response carries the id of that successor card account.

cardConfig.description:
The Pliant card configuration of this card.
This describes all features of this card in one single configuration, e.g. the type of the card and also the design of the card etc.
Please refer to the [guide section](/docs/card-entity) to learn more about possible values.

cardDesignId.description:
The unique identifier of the card design used for this card.
This field can only be set when creating virtual cards.
Available designs for a card config can be retrieved via the [available cards endpoint](/reference/get-available-cards).

label.description: Mandatory only for virtual cards with a `cardConfig` containing `VIRTUAL` or `TRAVEL`, the maximum length is 40 characters.

validityPeriod.description:
Number of months when card expires.
- Mandatory for `cardConfig` containing `VIRTUAL` and `TRAVEL`
- For `cardConfig` ending with `PHYSICAL` or `BLACK`: set to 36 months automatically
- For `cardConfig` ending with `SINGLE_USE`: set to 12 months automatically
- For `cardConfig` containing `INSURANCE`:
  - Physical insurance: set to 24 months automatically
  - Virtual insurance (excluding single-use): validated from enum, defaults to 36 months
  - Single-use insurance: set to 12 months automatically
For cards with fixed validity periods, user input is ignored.

validFrom.description: Optional field to describe a fixed date range in which the card is usable for purchases, replaces the `validityPeriod` if used. Outside of this date range, the card cannot be used for any purchases, only for zero-amount card-checks, and is shown with `status` `PENDING`. If not provided, the card is active immediately. Date needs to be provided as `yyyy-mm-dd` and is treated inclusive, meaning the provided date is already a valid day to use the card. If used, the parallel usage of card controls regarding `dates` and/or `times` is not allowed and the `validityPeriod` will be set to 36 months automatically. The earliest possible date is the current date. The `validFrom` date needs to be before the `validTo` date. The fields `validFrom`, `validTo` and `validTimezone` need to be used together, if used at all. This field can be [updated later](/reference/update-card-validity-period). This field must be `null` when issuing benefit cards.

validTo.description: Optional field to describe a fixed date range in which the card is usable for purchases, replaces the `validityPeriod` if used. After the specified date, the card is automatically terminated. If not provided, the card is active until the `validityPeriod` ends. Date needs to be provided as `yyyy-mm-dd` and is treated inclusive, meaning the card will be terminated one day after this date. If used, the parallel usage of card controls regarding `dates` and/or `times` is not allowed and the `validityPeriod` will be set to 36 months automatically. The earliest possible date is the current date. The latest possible date is the end date of the `validityPeriod`. The fields `validFrom`, `validTo` and `validTimezone` need to be used together, if used at all. This field can be [updated later](/reference/update-card-validity-period). This field must be `null` when issuing benefit cards.

validTimezone.description: Optional field to describe the timezone for the `validFrom` and `validTo` fields. This field is mandatory if `validFrom` and `validTo` fields are used. A list of valid timezones can be found in our [guide section](/docs/card-controls-1). This field can be [updated later](/reference/update-card-validity-period). This field must be `null` when issuing benefit cards.

maxTransactionCount.description:
:exclamation: IMPORTANT: if the `cardConfig` is `TRAVEL` and this field is not set, the **default value will be `5`**.
Optional field to describe the maximum number of transactions within the range of `1..999999999` that can be performed with this card.
If not provided, the card can be used for an unlimited number of transactions until the card expires.

limit.description: The limit of the card. The limit renews according to the `limitRenewFrequency` or never, if `limitRenewFrequency` is set to `TOTAL`. This limit can later be adjusted via the [update limit endpoint](/reference/update-card-limit). The limit can be up to the organization's overall limit. For instance an organization with a limit of 1,000,000 EUR can have a card with a limit up to 1,000,000 EUR. It is also possible to have more than one card with the maximum limit. For example you can have two cards each with a limit of 1,000,000 EUR. The card limits are not added up on creation, only the transactions happening on the card are added up and checked against the organization's overall limit. The limit must be `0` (of the card's currency) when issuing benefit cards.

value.description: The value of the monetary amount, converted to minor units of the currency. For instance 1.00 EUR is 100 cents, thus the value here is `100`. See our [guides](/docs/monetary-values) for more details about how to handle monetary amounts.

currency.description: The currency of the monetary amount in ISO 4217 format, for example `EUR` for Euro. This has to match the currency of the respective [card account](/docs/card-account)!

limitRenewFrequency.description:
The frequency of the card limit renewal.
* `DAILY` - The card limit is renewed every day
* `WEEKLY` - The card limit is renewed every week
* `MONTHLY` - The card limit is renewed every calendar month, this is the default setting.
* `QUARTERLY` - The card limit is renewed every calendar quarter.
* `ANNUAL` - The card limit is renewed every year.
* `TOTAL` - The card limit is never going to be renewed. After the limit is spent the card cannot be used anymore.

transactionLimit.description: The transaction limit of the card. Meaning the maximum amount of a single transaction. This is always below or equal to the `limit` of the card. This limit can later be adjusted via the [update limit endpoint](/reference/update-card-limit). The transaction limit can be up to the card's limit. For instance a card with a limit of 1,000 EUR can have a transaction limit up to 1,000 EUR. The transaction limit must be `0` (of the card's currency) when issuing benefit cards.

value.description: The value of the monetary amount, converted to minor units of the currency. For instance 1.00 EUR is 100 cents, thus the value here is `100`. See our [guides](/docs/monetary-values) for more details about how to handle monetary amounts.

currency.description: The currency of the monetary amount in ISO 4217 format, for example `EUR` for Euro. This has to match the currency of the respective [card account](/docs/card-account)!

When used, this replaces the [cardholder](/docs/cardholder-entity) first name, which normally is used on the card. The maximum length of `customFirstName` is 50 characters. If used, both fields (`customFirstName` and `customLastName`) have to be provided with at least one character each. It is important to note, that only the following characters are allowed for issuing cards: `A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`, `äöüÄÖÜ.-`

When used, this replaces the [cardholder](/docs/cardholder-entity) last name, which normally is used on the card. The maximum length of `customLastName` is 50 characters. If used, both fields (`customFirstName` and `customLastName`) have to be provided with at least one character each. It is important to note, that only the following characters are allowed for issuing cards: `A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`, `äöüÄÖÜ.-`

customFields.description: Optional custom fields which can be set on a card. A custom field may have a default value which will be copied to every transaction made with this card. You can identify a custom field either by its `id` or its `label`. If both are provided, the `id` will be used. You can also create new custom fields (of type `TEXT`) on-the-fly by providing a newly, unused label and the corresponding default value you want to set. So mainly two uses cases exist: 1. Use an existing custom field on the card, mostly identified via its `id`. 2. Create a new custom field (of type `TEXT`) on-the-fly via the `label` and set it on the card.

id.description: The id of the custom field, to identify an existing custom field which should be set on this card. Either `id` or `label` has to be provided. If both are provided, the `id` will be used.

label.description: The label of the custom field, to identify which custom field should be set on this card. Or, to create a new custom field on-the-fly, if the label is currently unused. Either `id` or `label` has to be provided. If both are provided, the `id` will be used.

defaultValue.description: The default value of the custom field to set on this card. This default value will be copied to every transaction made with this card. This is not the default value of the custom field itself, but the default value of the custom field on this card! The maximum length of the default value is 64kB.

deliverTo.description:
Optionally, specifies where the physical card should be delivered.
* `ORGANIZATION` - Ship to organization address (default)
* `CARDHOLDER` - Ship to cardholder's personal delivery address

This field is only applicable for physical cards.
If not provided, the card will be shipped to the organization address.


The request will fail if the cardholder's personal delivery address is not set and `deliverTo` is set to `CARDHOLDER`.

cardholder.description: Optional description of a new [cardholder](/docs/cardholder-entity) to be created alongside the card. If `cardholderId` is not provided, this field is required.

membershipType.description:
Defines how the cardholder is onboarded and accesses their cards.
`STANDARD` - Cardholders receive an invitation email to register, set up a password and MFA, and become registered members with access to the Pliant web app according to their assigned role.
`LIMITED` - For distributing cards via access links without requiring registration. This is also intended for direct customers sharing cards with recipients outside their organization. Cardholders do not receive a registration invitation and cannot access the Pliant web app. Instead, they access their cards through access links shared with them, with access limited to card-related functionality. The `GUEST` role is assigned automatically and does not need to be provided.
`EMBEDDED` - Reserved for partners embedding the cardholder experience in their own application. No invitation email is sent. The partner is responsible for obtaining acceptance of the terms and conditions and verifying the cardholder's phone number.
If not provided, `STANDARD` is applied. `LIMITED` and `EMBEDDED` always have to be requested explicitly.

validFrom.description: Optional field to describe a fixed date range in which the card is usable for purchases. Outside of this date range, the card cannot be used for any purchases, only for zero-amount card-checks, and is shown with `status` `PENDING`. If not provided, the card is active immediately. Date needs to be provided as `yyyy-mm-dd` and is treated inclusive, meaning the provided date is already a valid day to use the card. If used, the parallel usage of card controls regarding `dates` and/or `times` is not allowed and the `validityPeriod` will be set to 36 months automatically. The earliest possible date is the current date. The `validFrom` date needs to be before the `validTo` date. The fields `validFrom`, `validTo` and `validTimezone` need to be used together, if used at all.

If not provided, the card is active until the `validityPeriod` ends. Date needs to be provided as `yyyy-mm-dd` and is treated inclusive, meaning the card will be terminated one day after this date. If used, the parallel usage of card controls regarding `dates` and/or `times` is not allowed and the `validityPeriod` will be set to 36 months automatically. The latest possible date is the end date of the `validityPeriod`. The fields `validFrom`, `validTo` and `validTimezone` need to be used together, if used at all.

post.description:
Issue a new credit card for an existing or a new cardholder. A detailed explanation of different types and statuses can be found in our [guides](/docs/card-entity) section. Hint: you can also [replace](./replace-card) an existing card instead.
If the cardholder is in the invited state at the time of issuing the card, we will park the card issuing request and automatically issue the card once the cardholder is active.
Please be aware that card issuing is (as many other processes in Pliant's API) an [asynchronous process](/docs/core-concepts#mutating-data-happens-asynchronously). This means you need to rely on the callback for the card being active, before you can start using it.

cardholderId.description: The id of the [cardholder](/docs/cardholder-entity) to issue the card for. This cardholder needs to have a phone number, otherwise 3DS security mechanism during a purchase will not work. If not provided, you must provide a `cardholder` object to create a new cardholder as part of the card issuing process.

organizationId.description: The ID of the organization to issue the card for.

cardAccountId.description: The ID of the [card account](/docs/card-account) to issue the card for. If not provided, the card will be issued for the default [card account](/docs/card-account) of the organization. If the given card account has `status` `SUPERSEDED`, the request is transparently resolved to its successor (`supersededBy`) and the response carries the id of that successor card account.

cardConfig.description:
The Pliant card configuration of this card.
This describes all features of this card in one single configuration, e.g. the type of the card and also the design of the card etc.
Please refer to the [guide section](/docs/card-entity) to learn more about possible values.

cardDesignId.description:
The unique identifier of the card design used for this card.
This field can only be set when creating virtual cards.
Available designs for a card config can be retrieved via the [available cards endpoint](/reference/get-available-cards).

label.description: Mandatory only for virtual cards with a `cardConfig` containing `VIRTUAL` or `TRAVEL`, the maximum length is 40 characters.

purpose.description: Mandatory only for virtual cards with `cardConfig` ending with `SINGLE_USE`

validityPeriod.description:
Number of months when card expires.
- Mandatory for `cardConfig` containing `VIRTUAL` and `TRAVEL`
- For `cardConfig` ending with `PHYSICAL` or `BLACK`: set to 36 months automatically
- For `cardConfig` ending with `SINGLE_USE`: set to 12 months automatically
- For `cardConfig` containing `INSURANCE`:
  - Physical insurance: set to 24 months automatically
  - Virtual insurance (excluding single-use): validated from enum, defaults to 36 months
  - Single-use insurance: set to 12 months automatically
For cards with fixed validity periods, user input is ignored.

validFrom.description: Optional field to describe a fixed date range in which the card is usable for purchases, replaces the `validityPeriod` if used. Outside of this date range, the card cannot be used for any purchases, only for zero-amount card-checks, and is shown with `status` `PENDING`. If not provided, the card is active immediately. Date needs to be provided as `yyyy-mm-dd` and is treated inclusive, meaning the provided date is already a valid day to use the card. If used, the parallel usage of card controls regarding `dates` and/or `times` is not allowed and the `validityPeriod` will be set to 36 months automatically. The earliest possible date is the current date. The `validFrom` date needs to be before the `validTo` date. The fields `validFrom`, `validTo` and `validTimezone` need to be used together, if used at all. This field can be [updated later](/reference/update-card-validity-period). This field must be `null` when issuing benefit cards.

validTo.description: Optional field to describe a fixed date range in which the card is usable for purchases, replaces the `validityPeriod` if used. After the specified date, the card is automatically terminated. If not provided, the card is active until the `validityPeriod` ends. Date needs to be provided as `yyyy-mm-dd` and is treated inclusive, meaning the card will be terminated one day after this date. If used, the parallel usage of card controls regarding `dates` and/or `times` is not allowed and the `validityPeriod` will be set to 36 months automatically. The earliest possible date is the current date. The latest possible date is the end date of the `validityPeriod`. The fields `validFrom`, `validTo` and `validTimezone` need to be used together, if used at all. This field can be [updated later](/reference/update-card-validity-period). This field must be `null` when issuing benefit cards.

validTimezone.description: Optional field to describe the timezone for the `validFrom` and `validTo` fields. This field is mandatory if `validFrom` and `validTo` fields are used. A list of valid timezones can be found in our [guide section](/docs/card-controls-1). This field can be [updated later](/reference/update-card-validity-period). This field must be `null` when issuing benefit cards.

maxTransactionCount.description:
:exclamation: IMPORTANT: if the `cardConfig` is `TRAVEL` and this field is not set, the **default value will be `5`**.
Optional field to describe the maximum number of transactions within the range of `1..999999999` that can be performed with this card.
If not provided, the card can be used for an unlimited number of transactions until the card expires.

limit.description: The limit of the card. The limit renews according to the `limitRenewFrequency` or never, if `limitRenewFrequency` is set to `TOTAL`. This limit can later be adjusted via the [update limit endpoint](/reference/update-card-limit). The limit can be up to the organization's overall limit. For instance an organization with a limit of 1,000,000 EUR can have a card with a limit up to 1,000,000 EUR. It is also possible to have more than one card with the maximum limit. For example you can have two cards each with a limit of 1,000,000 EUR. The card limits are not added up on creation, only the transactions happening on the card are added up and checked against the organization's overall limit. The limit must be `0` (of the card's currency) when issuing benefit cards.

value.description: The value of the monetary amount, converted to minor units of the currency. For instance 1.00 EUR is 100 cents, thus the value here is `100`. See our [guides](/docs/monetary-values) for more details about how to handle monetary amounts.

currency.description: The currency of the monetary amount in ISO 4217 format, for example `EUR` for Euro. This has to match the currency of the respective [card account](/docs/card-account)!

limitRenewFrequency.description:
The frequency of the card limit renewal.
* `DAILY` - The card limit is renewed every day
* `WEEKLY` - The card limit is renewed every week
* `MONTHLY` - The card limit is renewed every calendar month, this is the default setting.
* `QUARTERLY` - The card limit is renewed every calendar quarter.
* `ANNUAL` - The card limit is renewed every year.
* `TOTAL` - The card limit is never going to be renewed. After the limit is spent the card cannot be used anymore.

transactionLimit.description: The transaction limit of the card. Meaning the maximum amount of a single transaction. This is always below or equal to the `limit` of the card. This limit can later be adjusted via the [update limit endpoint](/reference/update-card-limit). The transaction limit can be up to the card's limit. For instance a card with a limit of 1,000 EUR can have a transaction limit up to 1,000 EUR. The transaction limit must be `0` (of the card's currency) when issuing benefit cards.

value.description: The value of the monetary amount, converted to minor units of the currency. For instance 1.00 EUR is 100 cents, thus the value here is `100`. See our [guides](/docs/monetary-values) for more details about how to handle monetary amounts.

currency.description: The currency of the monetary amount in ISO 4217 format, for example `EUR` for Euro. This has to match the currency of the respective [card account](/docs/card-account)!

customFirstName.description: Optional first name on `TRAVEL` cards which will be used on the card. When used, this replaces the [cardholder](/docs/cardholder-entity) first name, which normally is used on the card. The maximum length of `customFirstName` is 50 characters. If used, both fields (`customFirstName` and `customLastName`) have to be provided with at least one character each. It is important to note, that only the following characters are allowed for issuing cards: `A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`, `äöüÄÖÜ.-`

customLastName.description: Optional last name on `TRAVEL` cards which will be used on the card. When used, this replaces the [cardholder](/docs/cardholder-entity) last name, which normally is used on the card. The maximum length of `customLastName` is 50 characters. If used, both fields (`customFirstName` and `customLastName`) have to be provided with at least one character each. It is important to note, that only the following characters are allowed for issuing cards: `A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`, `äöüÄÖÜ.-`

cardControls.description: Optionally, the card controls which will be applied to this card.

customFields.description: Optional custom fields which can be set on a card. A custom field may have a default value which will be copied to every transaction made with this card. You can identify a custom field either by its `id` or its `label`. If both are provided, the `id` will be used. You can also create new custom fields (of type `TEXT`) on-the-fly by providing a newly, unused label and the corresponding default value you want to set. So mainly two uses cases exist: 1. Use an existing custom field on the card, mostly identified via its `id`. 2. Create a new custom field (of type `TEXT`) on-the-fly via the `label` and set it on the card.

id.description: The id of the custom field, to identify an existing custom field which should be set on this card. Either `id` or `label` has to be provided. If both are provided, the `id` will be used.

label.description: The label of the custom field, to identify which custom field should be set on this card. Or, to create a new custom field on-the-fly, if the label is currently unused. Either `id` or `label` has to be provided. If both are provided, the `id` will be used.

defaultValue.description: The default value of the custom field to set on this card. This default value will be copied to every transaction made with this card. This is not the default value of the custom field itself, but the default value of the custom field on this card! The maximum length of the default value is 64kB.

teamId.description: The ID of the team to issue the card for.

copilots.description: Optional feature for `TRAVEL` cards. This feature allows to assign cardholders or teams as copilots to the card. The copilot also has access to the card and its card details alongside with the cardholder of the card itself.

deliverTo.description:
Optionally, specifies where the physical card should be delivered.
* `ORGANIZATION` - Ship to organization address (default)
* `CARDHOLDER` - Ship to cardholder's personal delivery address

This field is only applicable for physical cards.
If not provided, the card will be shipped to the organization address.


The request will fail if the cardholder's personal delivery address is not set and `deliverTo` is set to `CARDHOLDER`.

cardholder.description: Optional description of a new [cardholder](/docs/cardholder-entity) to be created alongside the card. If `cardholderId` is not provided, this field is required.

membershipType.description:
Defines how the cardholder is onboarded and accesses their cards.
`STANDARD` - Cardholders receive an invitation email to register, set up a password and MFA, and become registered members with access to the Pliant web app according to their assigned role.
`LIMITED` - For distributing cards via access links without requiring registration. This is also intended for direct customers sharing cards with recipients outside their organization. Cardholders do not receive a registration invitation and cannot access the Pliant web app. Instead, they access their cards through access links shared with them, with access limited to card-related functionality. The `GUEST` role is assigned automatically and does not need to be provided.
`EMBEDDED` - Reserved for partners embedding the cardholder experience in their own application. No invitation email is sent. The partner is responsible for obtaining acceptance of the terms and conditions and verifying the cardholder's phone number.
If not provided, `STANDARD` is applied. `LIMITED` and `EMBEDDED` always have to be requested explicitly.

salutation.description: The Salutation used for email communication.

email.description: The email address of the cardholder. This will be used for email communication. If a cardholder with this email address already exists, all the information from the existing cardholder will be used, the cardholder information sent in this request will be ignored.

firstName.description: The first name of the cardholder. This will be printed on credit cards as the cardholder. It is important to note, that only the following characters are allowed for issuing cards: `A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`, `äöüÄÖÜ.-` The combined length of first name and last name must not exceed 24 characters. One additional character is reserved for the space inserted between them when displayed on the card (25 characters in total).

lastName.description: The last name of the cardholder. This will be printed on credit cards as the cardholder. It is important to note, that only the following characters are allowed for issuing cards: `A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`, `äöüÄÖÜ.-` The combined length of first name and last name must not exceed 24 characters. One additional character is reserved for the space inserted between them when displayed on the card (25 characters in total).

language.description: Used for setting the language in Pliant apps as well as for email communication.

nationality.description: The nationality of the cardholder (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2).

roles.description:
Roles of the cardholder to be created. Usually, the regular cardholder uses the `CARDHOLDER` role, granting them full access to the Pliant platform. Alternatively the `GUEST` role can be provided to give the cardholder limited access to Pliant apps.
Required for `STANDARD` memberships. For `LIMITED` the `GUEST` role is assigned automatically and cannot be combined with any other role, so you do not need to provide this property. For `EMBEDDED` roles do not apply and `CARDHOLDER` is used when none is provided.

validFrom.description: Optional field to describe a fixed date range in which the card is usable for purchases. Outside of this date range, the card cannot be used for any purchases, only for zero-amount card-checks, and is shown with `status` `PENDING`. If not provided, the card is active immediately. Date needs to be provided as `yyyy-mm-dd` and is treated inclusive, meaning the provided date is already a valid day to use the card. If used, the parallel usage of card controls regarding `dates` and/or `times` is not allowed and the `validityPeriod` will be set to 36 months automatically. The earliest possible date is the current date. The `validFrom` date needs to be before the `validTo` date. The fields `validFrom`, `validTo` and `validTimezone` need to be used together, if used at all.

validTo.description: Optional field to describe a fixed date range in which the card is usable for purchases. After the specified date, the card is automatically terminated. If not provided, the card is active until the `validityPeriod` ends. Date needs to be provided as `yyyy-mm-dd` and is treated inclusive, meaning the card will be terminated one day after this date. If used, the parallel usage of card controls regarding `dates` and/or `times` is not allowed and the `validityPeriod` will be set to 36 months automatically. The latest possible date is the end date of the `validityPeriod`. The fields `validFrom`, `validTo` and `validTimezone` need to be used together, if used at all.

validTimezone.description: Optional field to describe the timezone for the `validFrom` and `validTo` fields. This field is mandatory if `validFrom` and `validTo` fields are used. A list of valid timezones can be found in our [guide section](/docs/card-controls-1).

maxTransactionCount.description: Optional field to describe the maximum number of transactions within the range of `1..999999999` that can be performed with this card. If not provided, the card can be used for an unlimited number of transactions until the card expires.

clickToPayInfo.description:
Click to Pay enrollment information for this card. Only present for Visa cards that support Click to Pay.
This object may be `null` if Click to Pay is not supported generally (e.g., per country), but normally it will be present with a `status` of `NOT_SUPPORTED` if the card type doesn't support Click to Pay (e.g., Mastercard or Travel Purchasing Cards).

status.description:
The Click to Pay enrollment status of the card.
* `NOT_SUPPORTED` - Card type doesn't support Click to Pay (e.g., Mastercard or Travel Purchasing Cards)
* `NOT_ENROLLED` - Card is eligible but not enrolled in Click to Pay
* `PENDING` - Card enrollment is awaiting the cardholder's Click to Pay member enrollment to complete
* `ENROLLED` - Card is currently enrolled in Click to Pay

limitRenewFrequency.description:
The renewal frequency of this additional limit. `PER_TRANSACTION` is only valid for additional limits, not for the card's primary limit.
* `PER_TRANSACTION` - Limit applies to each individual transaction.
* `DAILY` - The limit is renewed every day.
* `WEEKLY` - The limit is renewed every week.
* `MONTHLY` - The limit is renewed every calendar month.
* `QUARTERLY` - The limit is renewed every calendar quarter.
* `ANNUAL` - The limit is renewed every year.
* `TOTAL` - The limit is never renewed. Once spent, no further transactions are allowed under this limit.

get.description:
Returns a list of cards. You can use the `limit`, `page`, `sortBy` and `sortDirection` parameters to filter and sort the results.

**This endpoint has changed in comparison to the previous version of the API.** The following changes were made:
- changed the enumeration for the status field in the response body

parameters.name: organizationId
parameters.description: The ID of the organization to filter by.

parameters.name: cardAccountId
parameters.description: The ID of the card account to filter by. A card always carries the card account it is currently assigned to. Once a card has been reassigned (see the `CARD_REASSIGNED` callback), it is only returned for its new card account, not for the superseded one.

parameters.description: A list of statuses of cards to filter by.

parameters.description: The ID of the [cardholder](/docs/cardholder-entity) to filter by.

parameters.name: fromDate
parameters.description: The `from` date to filter by as zero-offset UTC time. The date boundary is inclusive. Meaning we compare with `>=`.

parameters.name: toDate
parameters.description: The `to` date to filter by as zero-offset UTC time. The date boundary is inclusive. Meaning we compare with `<=`.

parameters.description: The date field to filter by if `fromDate` and `toDate` are present.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of items to return per page. The default value if not provided is 100, the maximum allowed value is 1000.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page number to return, starting with 0, this counts up to the total number of pages. The total number of pages is determined by the total number of records divided by the limit.

parameters.name: sortBy
parameters.description: The field to sort by.

parameters.description: The direction to sort by.
